channel.title: Crypto Evidence Daily
channel.description: Independent daily crypto reporting for researchers and analysts, explaining protocol changes, market structure and policy through primary sources.

item.title: An NFT Is a Token Record, Not the Asset It Points To
item.description: An NFT proves control of a unique token entry, while its contract, metadata and outside agreements determine which rights, if any, come with it.

item.title: Digital Collectibles Prove Control, Not Legal Ownership
item.description: Digital collectibles use token IDs, wallet addresses and signed transfers to prove on-chain control, while media rights and bridge risks remain separate.

item.title: How a Block Stops the Same Crypto Being Spent Twice
item.description: Blocks prevent duplicate spends by ordering valid transactions, rejecting conflicts and making reversal increasingly costly as consensus builds on the ledger.

item.title: How Algorithmic Pegs Absorb—or Amplify—Market Imbalances
item.description: Algorithmic pegs use arbitrage to rebalance supply, but their resilience depends on liquid collateral, credible redemptions and loss-bearing capacity.

item.title: Cross-Chain Assets Make Metadata a Governance Question
item.description: Cross-chain wrappers can preserve token identity across networks while leaving code, display data and redemption claims under separate, changeable control.

item.title: Ethereum’s 2026 Proof Push Moves Cost Off Verifiers
item.description: Proof aggregation replaces repeated on-chain checks with one succinct verdict, cutting verifier work while shifting computation and liveness risk to provers.

item.title: Bybit’s $1.5 Billion Theft Clarified Wallet Control
item.description: A wallet's controller is whoever can authorize its next transaction; custody determines whether exchange failure or key loss becomes the holder's risk.

item.title: Ethereum Checkpoints Put a Price on Reversing History
item.description: Checkpoints turn repeated validator votes into explicit settlement boundaries, reducing reorg risk while trading instant certainty for liveness and delay.

item.title: Limit Orders Wait for a Price; Swaps Take the Market
item.description: A swap trades now against available liquidity, while a limit order waits for a target price, shifting execution risk, costs and control between users.

item.title: Why Ethereum Nonces Prevent Duplicate Transactions
item.description: A nonce makes each account transaction usable once, blocking replay at consensus while imposing strict ordering and occasional delays on Ethereum users.

item.title: Account Abstraction Makes Ethereum Wallets Programmable
item.description: Ethereum’s account abstraction makes wallets programmable, enabling batched actions and sponsored gas while shifting trust into code, relayers and paymasters.

item.title: On-Chain Data Shows Behavior, Not Motive
item.description: On-chain data works best when balances, fees and repeated actions are read together; transaction counts alone can mistake cheaper activity for demand.

item.title: IPFS CID Profiles Make Silent File Changes Easier to Catch
item.description: IPFS’s new CID profiles standardize file packaging, making identical data reproducible across tools while exposing any changed byte under a new address.

item.title: Which Domain Names Resolve to Wallet Addresses in 2026?
item.description: In 2026, .eth, .sol and app-specific names can route crypto payments, but resolution still depends on records, networks and the sender’s wallet support.

item.title: What Bonding Curves Really Change About Token Pricing
item.description: Bonding curves create instant liquidity by pricing inventory with code, but early entry, slippage and fee design decide who captures the launch premium.

item.title: CME’s 24/7 Shift Clarifies What Crypto Options Promise
item.description: CME’s move to round-the-clock crypto derivatives sharpens a basic distinction: option buyers purchase a choice, while sellers accept the obligation.

item.title: Standard Chartered brings spot Bitcoin and Ether to UAE desks
item.description: Standard Chartered launched deliverable Bitcoin and Ether spot trading in Dubai, giving institutions a regulated bank route from execution to custody.

item.title: Circle agrees to buy Tazapay for 100-market payout reach
item.description: Circle agreed to buy Tazapay, adding $25 billion in annualized flows and local rails in 100-plus markets to its bid to make USDC payment infrastructure.

item.title: 24X Executes First Spot Bitcoin Trade With Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered took liquidity from Cumberland on 24X, proving live bank-grade execution while leaving volume, spreads and settlement undisclosed.

item.title: SoFi and Payward Tie 24/7 Dollar Settlement to Kraken
item.description: The pact gives Kraken institutions round-the-clock dollar settlement and SoFi another crypto-liquidity route, but adoption and execution gains remain unproven.
